newsitem.title: USA: World Bank to lend Bosnia $32 million.
newsitem.headline: World Bank to lend Bosnia $32 million.

text.p: The World Bank said on Monday it had approved three loans totalling $32 million to help Bosnia put its war-ravaged economy back together.
The largest, for $15 million, will be used to rebuild hospitals and purchase medical equipment and supplies. Italy is kicking in $5.2 million in co-financing to the project.

The Bank set aside $10 million to help Bosnia attract foreign private financing by guaranteeing investors against political risks, including the possibility of new hostilities. Switzerland is contributiong $7.5 million to that efforts.

Antoher $7 million in Bank money will be used to help war widows, former soldiers and returning refugees set up their own businesses through microenterprise loans. Italy is contributing an additional $3.3 million to that effort.
The World Bank said all three credits were being provided through its International Development Association affiliate, which lends money at no interest charge to the world's poorest countries.
